analysis: This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md; no executable code or security control is modified. The patch adds a paragraph (head ~1118-1128) and one error-table row (head 1517). The paragraph says a Jinja `raise_exception` at request time maps to HTTP 500 (`jinja_template`). It says Flash-Next and Qwen3.8-27B templates accept only low/medium/xhigh reasoning effort while thinking is on. Other active efforts return a typed HTTP 400 `client_error` from `Qwen4SupportPolicy.validateReasoningContext` before rendering. It also says media preparation rethrows typed request errors rather than wrapping them as a retryable 503. Security relevance is availability and fault attribution (TB-002, ADV-002): a consumer-triggerable template rejection is reclassified from provider fault to client error. That plausibly reduces provider-fault misattribution, which could affect provider reputation or routing, and does not weaken confidentiality or authorization. I could not verify the referenced source (Qwen4SupportPolicy.swift, MediaIngest or scheduler paths) because it was not supplied. Whether the implementation matches the doc is an unverified contract and is a coverage limit, not a finding. The supplied head text for the rest of the document (Nemotron Super slot, prefix cache bank, MTP, deadlines) is existing content I only skimmed. The visible portions do not change T-041 posture: prefix reuse is scoped by authenticated cache scope, with no scope meaning no reuse or publish. The only changed-range content I saw is the reasoning-effort paragraph and table row, and it does not touch the cache, attestation, encryption or billing boundaries. No new attack surface, invalidated assumption or threat-model gap was identified. The later-hunk text of the patch (truncated after the table row) was not fully visible.
